newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to investigate aid to France's SFP.
newsitem.headline: EU to investigate aid to France's SFP.

text.p: The European Commission is set to begin an examination on Wednesday of French plans to help loss-making SFP film studios with a total of around 2.5 billion francs ($443 million), EU sources said on Tuesday.

"It is aid which has to be approved by the Commission," one source said, stressing that the European Union executive normally opened so-called state aid procedures to determine whether it could clear planned state support.

Of the total amount, a small part had already been granted to the Societe Francaise de Production et de Creation Audiovisuelle. "The main part is not yet granted, (it) will be legal if the Commission accepts it," he said.
It was too early to speculate on the outcome of the investigation, which could last three to four months. But he said France had a "decent, solid plan" to restructure the firm.
"So normally when the Commission gets a plan which shows that the company is viable, that the company can get on further without aid, normally the Commission accepts that," he said.
Of the 2.5 billion, 1.2 billion is intended to be a capital injection to pay for restructuring. The rest is to reduce the company's indebtedness, the source said.

The French government said late last year it planned to sell SFP, which produces live coverage of events for French television and also makes television and cinema films, to Generale des Eaux and Havas.
